title: Bethel Christian ave., Laurel Hill Historic District
summary: The Bethel-Christian Avenue-Laurel Hill Historic District (BCALH) was established and recognized by the Town of Brookhaven in 2005. It is a half-mile long stretch of Christian Avenue that includes the homes of several mixed heritage Native American and African American families as well as Bethel AME Church of Setauket, Laurel Hill Cemetery, and the Irving Hart Memorial Legion Hall. why_this_matters: Established in 2005, this half-mile historic district preserves the Bethel AME Church, Laurel Hill Cemetery, and the homes of tightly knit families of mixed Native American and African American descent. Acknowledging these shared neighborhoods challenges the harmful myth of Native disappearance, illustrating how Indigenous people adapted, intermarried, and built enduring institutions to survive centuries of marginalization.
history_content: Neighborhood History The Bethel-Christian Avenue-Laurel Hill Historic District connects Setalcott and African American history in a long-standing mixed-heritage community. Its value is not only architectural; it also carries family networks, landholding, worship, and resistance to erasure in Setauket. Interpretation stays at the historic-district level and avoids identifying private homes or nonpublic archaeological locations.
